turn: I finished matching amended notices to their originals. In src/match/amendments.py, link_corrigenda now pairs each CORR notice with the notice named in its amends field, and it skips any whose target isn't in the batch. The new apply_corrigendum then copies the corrigendum's changed fields onto the original and ignores fields set to None, so a blank value can't erase real data. I haven't run the code or any tests. I only re-read the two functions against the cases I had in mind: a corrigendum with a valid target, one with a missing target, and one that has None values. In the same commit I made one small unplanned fix. The date parser in the loader crashed on notice dates with trailing whitespace, so I now strip them before parsing. Next I'll start "Group matched pairs into duplicate sets".

sidefix.title: Strip whitespace before parsing notice dates
sidefix.what: The loader's date parser crashed on notice dates with trailing whitespace, so the value is now stripped before parsing.
